It distinguishes itself from image-space methods by processing geometry directly, allowing for precise hidden line removal and independent stroke stylization before compositing [S2].

The evidence explicitly describes an 'object-space line rendering approach' (which corresponds to processing geometry directly, as opposed to image-space methods). It lists the steps as 'geometry data preparation, line extraction, stroke generation, hidden line removal, and stroke stylization.' It details the Hidden Line Removal (HLR) process using a z-buffer and states that stylization (changing width, saturation, color, texture) is applied to visible strokes. Furthermore, it notes that edge extraction and stroke generation are independent from the final rendering steps, allowing for independent stylization before compositing (specifically mentioning combining with surface rendering later). All specific claims in the statement are present in the source text.

Silhouette rendering is an object-space line rendering technique that extracts and stylizes significant edges (silhouettes and feature lines) from volumetric or surface data to enhance perceptual clarity and context [S2][S1, book].

The claim is fully supported by the provided evidence. Source [S2] explicitly defines silhouette rendering as an 'object-space line rendering approach' that involves 'extracting significant edges (silhouettes and feature lines)' and applying 'stroke stylization'. It also details the process of Hidden Line Removal (HLR) to determine visibility. Source [S1] confirms the purpose of this technique, stating it is used to 'indicate context objects' and 'discriminate two classes of objects' to help users recognize specific features (like lymph nodes touching critical structures), which aligns with the claim's assertion that it enhances 'perceptual clarity and context'.
